_comment: 30 day-sets. morning = 6:00 AM ET, midday = 1:30 PM ET, evening = 6:00 PM ET. No speaker in the framing lines; quotations carry their own attribution. Day 1 morning and day 15 evening carry the brand + STOP tag that matches the registered sample messages.

days.morning: "Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking." - Marcus Aurelius. Daily Encouragement Messages - reply STOP to end.
days.midday: A pause counts as a plan. Three slow breaths, wherever this finds you. Nothing else is required.
days.evening: One good minute happened today. Find it and hold it a moment before the day closes.

days.morning: "No need to hurry. No need to sparkle. No need to be anybody but oneself." - Virginia Woolf, A Room of One's Own
days.midday: Step outside for the length of one song. The air is different out there, and that is the entire point.
days.evening: Name one thing handled today that nobody saw. It still counts. Often it counted most.

days.morning: "Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things." - Epictetus, Enchiridion
days.midday: Whatever anyone else is doing today is their weather. Set it down. Drink a glass of water.
days.evening: What was easier today than it would have been a year ago? There is usually something.

days.morning: "You do not have to be good. You only have to let the soft animal of your body love what it loves." - Mary Oliver, Wild Geese
days.midday: No task today. Just notice five things within reach that are pleasant. That is the whole exercise.
days.evening: Today asked for a lot or a little. Either way it is closed now, and rest is allowed.

days.morning: "Nothing can bring you peace but yourself." - Ralph Waldo Emerson, Self-Reliance
days.midday: Peace is portable. Two minutes sitting near anything green, a tree or a houseplant, will do.
days.evening: One thing worth being proud of today, however small. Say it plainly, with no qualifier after it.

days.morning: "Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: to choose one's attitude in any given set of circumstances." - Viktor Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning
days.midday: Choosing is available even now, even tired. Choose one small comfort and take it without arguing.
days.evening: The day got carried. That is not a low bar. Some days it is the only bar that matters.

days.morning: "The curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change." - Carl Rogers, On Becoming a Person
days.midday: Nothing about right now needs fixing. A hand somewhere warm, and a breath out longer than the breath in.
days.evening: Was there a moment today that felt easy? Those moments are data, not accidents.

days.morning: "We suffer more often in imagination than in reality." - Seneca, Letters to Lucilius
days.midday: Most of what is being worried about is not in the room. Look around the actual room. It is calmer.
days.evening: One worry from this morning that never arrived. There is almost always one worth noting.

days.morning: "In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer." - Albert Camus, Return to Tipasa
days.midday: Warmth is a strategy, not a luxury. Tea, a blanket, sun through a window. Five minutes of it.
days.evening: Something good is still in there, running quietly, whether or not it was visible today.

days.morning: "Caring for myself is not self-indulgence, it is self-preservation." - Audre Lorde, A Burst of Light
days.midday: One kind thing, done for no reason, aimed inward. It does not need to be productive.
days.evening: Who got taken care of today? If the answer includes the person reading this, that is the win.

days.morning: "Be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart. Live the questions now." - Rainer Maria Rilke, Letters to a Young Poet
days.midday: Not everything has to be decided today. Set one question down for later and go do something ordinary.
days.evening: Unsolved is not the same as failing. Most good things stay unsolved for a long while first.

days.morning: "Let everything happen to you: beauty and terror. Just keep going. No feeling is final." - Rainer Maria Rilke
days.midday: Whatever this feeling is, it has an expiration date. Wait it out somewhere comfortable.
days.evening: This morning's mood and this evening's mood are different. That is the proof that weather moves.

days.morning: "You are the sky. Everything else is just the weather." - Pema Chodron
days.midday: Weather passes over. Two minutes at a window, letting it pass without any commentary.
days.evening: Nothing that happened today changed what is actually there. It only changed the forecast.

days.morning: "The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself." - Michel de Montaigne, Essays
days.midday: Belonging to oneself looks like this: one small choice today made purely on preference.
days.evening: One thing chosen today for no reason but wanting it. That is the muscle, and it grows quietly.

days.morning: "What other people think of me is none of my business." - Wayne Dyer
days.midday: Somebody's opinion is doing laps rent free. Evict it. Go make a cup of something warm.
days.evening: Whose approval turned out not to be needed today? Notice how the day went anyway. Daily Encouragement Messages - reply STOP to end, HELP for help.

days.morning: "Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?" - Mary Oliver, The Summer Day
days.midday: The question is not urgent today. One small pleasant thing is enough of an answer for now.
days.evening: Even a quiet day is spent life, and spent well if any part of it was enjoyed.

days.morning: "He who knows he has enough is rich." - Lao Tzu, Tao Te Ching
days.midday: Find one thing already owned that is genuinely good. Looking at it counts as the exercise.
days.evening: Was anything today actually missing, or only quieter than wanted? The difference matters.

days.morning: "You will love again the stranger who was your self. Feast on your life." - Derek Walcott, Love After Love
days.midday: Eat something today that is enjoyed rather than efficient. That is the whole instruction.
days.evening: The stranger in the mirror is old company. Worth a nod tonight. She has been through a lot.

days.morning: "I can be changed by what happens to me. But I refuse to be reduced by it." - Maya Angelou, Letter to My Daughter
days.midday: Changed is fine. Changed is expected. A short walk, and let the change stay neutral for a minute.
days.evening: Nothing today made anyone smaller. Different, maybe. Not smaller.

days.morning: "Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes, including you." - Anne Lamott
days.midday: Ten minutes unplugged. Phone down, eyes closed or out a window. Restarting is a real technique.
days.evening: Rest taken today was not time lost. It is the thing that made the rest of it possible.

days.morning: "Who looks outside, dreams; who looks inside, awakes." - Carl Jung
days.midday: One minute of checking in rather than checking out. How is it in there, honestly? No fixing required.
days.evening: Naming a feeling makes it smaller. Name today's once, then let it go to bed.

days.morning: "Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity." - Simone Weil
days.midday: Sixty seconds of full attention on one ordinary thing. A tree, a cup, a sound. That is all.
days.evening: What got noticed today that would usually be missed? The noticing is the practice.

days.morning: "We must be willing to let go of the life we planned so as to have the life that is waiting for us." - Joseph Campbell
days.midday: The waiting life needs no decision today. It only needs a little room. Sit somewhere new.
days.evening: Plans changed. That is not the same as plans failing. Something else is still arriving.

days.morning: "I come into the peace of wild things who do not tax their lives with forethought of grief." - Wendell Berry
days.midday: Find something alive outside - a bird, a tree, a weed in the sidewalk - and watch it a minute.
days.evening: The wild things had an ordinary day too. Ordinary is the goal, not the consolation prize.

days.morning: "Talk to yourself like you would to someone you love." - Brene Brown
days.midday: Whatever was just said internally, say it again the way it would be said to a good friend.
days.evening: Was the inside voice kind today? If not, tomorrow issues a fresh one. They reset overnight.

days.morning: "Breathing in, I calm my body. Breathing out, I smile." - Thich Nhat Hanh, The Miracle of Mindfulness
days.midday: The sanctuary is available now and requires no travel. Thirty seconds with the eyes closed.
days.evening: It was in there all day, whether or not it got used. It will be there tomorrow too.

days.morning: "Instructions for living a life: Pay attention. Be astonished. Tell about it." - Mary Oliver, Sometimes
days.midday: One astonishing small thing today. Low bar on purpose. Light through something usually qualifies.
days.evening: Tell someone one thing from today, or write it down. It makes the day exist twice.

days.morning: "Happiness depends upon ourselves." - Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics
days.midday: Depends upon, not demanded of. One small pleasant thing, freely chosen, is the whole assignment.
days.evening: Where did today's happiness actually come from? Usually somewhere smaller than expected.

days.morning: "Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life." - Seneca, Letters to Lucilius
days.midday: This one day is a whole life. A few minutes of it spent on something purely enjoyable.
days.evening: One separate life, completed. Tomorrow gets its own, with no debts carried over.

days.morning: "The privilege of a lifetime is being who you are." - Joseph Campbell
days.midday: Being who you are takes no effort today. Five minutes sitting somewhere pleasant, being it.
days.evening: A month of mornings like this one. Whatever changed, changed slowly and from the inside.
